summary: Add ForeignKey constraint on account_user.referrer_id referencing account_user.id using an expand SQL stage to clear orphan values and add the constraint, deploy the new version with apply migration, retire the old version, and run a contract stage after retirement to verify FK integrity. Note column consistency is preserved as no SQL targets the note column.
write_consistency: The old version omits referrer_id on INSERT, receiving NULL via database default; the new version includes referrer_id with valid FK references. The FK constraint is added on a nullable column after invalid references are cleared, so both versions' writes are compatible. Note column untouched.
revision_notes: Revised from previous plan to use 'apply' migration instead of 'state_only' to avoid django_migration_is_state_only failure caused by the new version's migration adding a note column. Expand stage now clears orphans and adds FK in two statements. Contract stage placed after retire_old as required. No rollback_check needed.

stages.description: Set orphan referrer_id values to NULL and add ForeignKey constraint on account_user.referrer_id referencing account_user.id.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET referrer_id = NULL WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL AND referrer_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM account_user);
ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT fk_account_user_referrer FOREIGN KEY (referrer_id) REFERENCES account_user (id);

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version; it will no longer serve traffic against the database.
Verify the FK constraint is enforced and no invalid referrer references remain after old version retirement.
sql: SELECT referrer_id FROM account_user WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL AND referrer_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM account_user) LIMIT 1;
